title: entitopia metrics
description: What a project measures about its own scored pairs. Metric names are load-bearing: they are the keys of committed baseline and expectation files, so renaming one breaks every comparison already recorded against it.

baseline.description: Project-relative path to the committed baseline this project compares against. A project that has not taken its first baseline yet legitimately has none, so an absent file is a warning rather than a failure.

name.description: Key in the emitted record, and therefore in every baseline and expectation file. Not cosmetic.

filter.description: Which pairs this metric counts. Absent means every pair.

distinct.description: Dotted path whose unique values are counted, instead of counting pairs. A pair missing the path contributes nothing rather than a null bucket.

ratio.description: Computed from two other metrics after the pass over pairs, so it may name a metric declared later. A zero denominator yields 0.0, never NaN — NaN is not valid JSON and would poison the baseline it was written into.

not.description: A metric counts pairs, counts distinct values, or divides two other metrics — never two of those at once.

predicate.description: Exactly one test, or none at all to match every pair. The menu is closed: a predicate name nobody implemented must fail loudly, because a typo that quietly matches nothing reports a metric of zero as though it had been measured.

gap_between.description: Inclusive on both ends. A null gap never matches: an unparseable date is not evaluable, which is not the same as outside the window.

matched_identity_equals.description: Set equality after restricting to identity signals, so a corroborating signal firing alongside does not change the answer.

fields_equal.description: Both sides carry the same NON-NULL value for this summary field. Two records that both lack the field are not equal.
